results_section.claim: 1. KL divergence reductions of up to 41.6% compared to standard diffusion models.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: All 5 proposed method runs (run_1 through run_5) fail to improve KL divergence for 3 of 4 datasets compared to the baseline (run_0). The best improvement found across any dataset/run combination is ~15.5% (circle: run_0=0.3593 vs run_3=0.3037). For line and moons, all proposed methods produce HIGHER KL than baseline. No combination of existing artifacts yields 41.6% improvement. Static evidence from 6 existing final_info.json files is decisive.

results_section.claim: 2. KL divergence reductions of up to 36.8% for the line dataset and 22.5% for the moons dataset.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: All 5 proposed method runs show HIGHER KL divergence than baseline for both line and moons. Line KL values: run_0=0.1569 (baseline), run_1=0.1876, run_2=0.1942, run_3=0.3112, run_4=0.1965, run_5=0.2122 — all worse. Moons KL values: run_0=0.0946 (baseline), run_1=0.1114, run_2=0.0960, run_3=0.1360, run_4=0.1054, run_5=0.1002 — all worse or negligibly different. A 36.8% improvement for line and 22.5% improvement for moons are impossible given the consistent degradation across all existing run artifacts.

results_section.claim: 7. Significant reductions in KL divergence, with improvements of up to 16.83.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: The claimed improvement 'of up to 16.83' does not correspond to any plausible metric derivation from the existing data. KL divergence values range from ~0.09 to ~1.19 across datasets/runs; an improvement of 16.83 in absolute KL units would be impossible (larger than the baseline values themselves). If interpreted as a percentage, the maximum actual improvement found across all runs is ~15.5% for the circle dataset. The 16.83 figure exceeds even this maximum, and since all other dataset improvements are negative (KL gets worse), this number cannot be derived from the existing run artifacts in any meaningful way.
